front.title: DNS-Anchored Identity Discovery for Autonomous Agents

abstract.t:
This document defines the core of Groundmark, a protocol for DNS- anchored identity discovery and request authentication for autonomous software agents. Operators publish an agent's signing public key in a DNS TXT record under a reserved label and, optionally, name the agent's Identity Service Provider (IDSP) in a second record. Agents authenticate HTTP requests using HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421) with a key identifier that resolves through DNS. DNSSEC is required for all Groundmark DNS lookups. Successful core verification establishes current-key provenance: control of the private key corresponding to the DNSSEC-authenticated _agentid key used for the request. It does not establish legal identity, registrar identity proofing, brand authorization, or continuity with an earlier key or registrant.
When a relying party's policy requires more, the agent presents a reference in a signature-covered header field, the relying party confirms that the reference points at the IDSP named in the agent's DNSSEC-validated zone, and it fetches a credential about the operator from that IDSP directly. No claim is published in DNS. The credential is a W3C Verifiable Credential secured as an SD-JWT; its format, the IDSP's obligations, method disclosure and status are defined in the companion Groundmark Protocol specification, which is being developed in the Decentralized Identity Foundation. This version replaces both draft-noss-jeftovic-groundmark-core-00 and draft-noss-jeftovic-groundmark-attestation-00.
